question: A 62-year-old woman comes to the physician because of increasing blurring of vision in both eyes. She says that the blurring has made it difficult to read, although she has noticed that she can read a little better if she holds the book below or above eye level. She also requires a bright light to look at objects. She reports that her symptoms began 8 years ago and have gradually gotten worse over time. She has hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Current medications include glyburide and lisinopril. When looking at an Amsler grid, she says that the lines in the center appear wavy and bent. An image of her retina, as viewed through fundoscopy is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

paths: (Amsler chart assessment)-DIAGNOSES->(Disorder of macula of retina)-CAUSES->(Age related macular degeneration)
(Amsler chart assessment)-DIAGNOSES->(Disorder of macula of retina)-CAUSES->(Age related macular degeneration)

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus -> increased risk of retinal complications -> 80% CHAIN: Blurring of vision, difficulty reading, need for bright light -> symptoms of macular degeneration -> 70% CHAIN: Amsler grid shows wavy and bent lines in the center -> characteristic of age-related macular degeneration -> 90% CHAIN: Fundoscopy reveals findings consistent with age-related macular degeneration -> likely diagnosis -> 80%
enhanced_information: The patient's symptoms of blurring vision, difficulty reading, need for bright light, and Amsler grid showing wavy and bent lines in the center are highly suggestive of age-related macular degeneration. Fundoscopy findings consistent with this diagnosis further support the likelihood of age-related macular degeneration as the most probable diagnosis in this case.
analysis: The patient's symptoms of blurring vision, difficulty reading, need for bright light, and Amsler grid showing wavy and bent lines in the center are highly indicative of age-related macular degeneration (AMD). The fundoscopy findings align with AMD, supporting this diagnosis. Given the patient's age, symptoms, and clinical presentation, AMD is the most likely diagnosis.
